fields.notes: DALI (IEC 62386) is a low-voltage, application-layer building-automation protocol that contains NO confidentiality, integrity, authentication, or access-control mechanisms at the protocol level. Specifically: (a) forward frames travel in cleartext on the 2-wire DC bus — anyone with wire access can sniff and decode every transaction; (b) there is no per-frame signing — a man-in-the-middle on the bus can alter address bytes, data bytes, or destructive STORE DTR AS ... commands undetectably; (c) there is no authentication of the control device — any device that can drive the bus can issue commands (including destructive RESET / STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS / PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS); (d) no replay protection — captured forward frames can be replayed at any later time; (e) no privacy of QUERY responses — any sniffer sees every backward frame. The two-strike commit rule (destructive commands sent twice within 100 ms) is an integrity-mitigation against electrical noise but provides no defence against malicious traffic.
practical_mitigations: Physical security — DALI bus runs inside the luminaire / ceiling plenum, restricting physical attacker access.
Galvanic isolation — opto-isolators between bus and microcontroller block injected high voltage / surge.
Network segmentation — DALI bus is bridged to the BMS via a router / gateway that can enforce policy at the IP / KNX side.
Bus power supply with fault current limit — bounded current (≤ 250 mA) limits the damage of a deliberate short.
PHYS_MIN_LEVEL clamp — Minimum Level cannot be set below the physical floor, preventing malicious dimming-to-zero attacks on critical lighting.
Power On Level + System Failure Level — bus-level survivability defaults ensure lights come back on after an interruption.
DALI-2 era certification — DiiA testing weeds out non-compliant gear; legitimate certified gear obeys the published spec.
fields.non_iec62386_security_extensions: Some vendors layer encryption / authentication on top of DALI via the User-Defined extension command ranges (commands 65..72 and 100..110), via memory bank 1+ writes carrying signed tokens, or via DALI-to-IP gateways that translate to authenticated MQTT / TLS. None of this is portable across vendors. There is no IEC-published 'DALI Secure' analogue to Modbus-Secure or BACnet-Secure as of IEC 62386-2014; DALI for safety-critical or security-relevant lighting (e.g. emergency / mass-notification) relies on physical isolation + redundant networks rather than on bus-level cryptography.
